chapters.title: The field of play
chapters.body:
Inspect the surface, markings, goals and corner flags before kick-off. Safety comes first: unsecured goals or a dangerous surface must be resolved before play.

The boundary line belongs to the area it encloses. A ball touching the touchline has not yet left the field.

chapters.title: The ball
chapters.body:
Use a suitable spherical ball and check its condition and pressure. Keep replacement balls ready under the referee’s control.

If a ball becomes defective during ordinary play, stop, replace it and use a dropped ball. A defective ball during a restart can require the restart to be retaken.

chapters.title: The players
chapters.body:
Check the team list, substitutes and competition rules. The normal format has at most eleven players per team, including a goalkeeper. Seven is the usual minimum; temporary protocol exceptions exist.

In 2026/27, a substituted player normally has ten seconds to leave. An unjustified delay means the substitute waits until the first stoppage after one minute of resumed play.

chapters.title: Players’ equipment
chapters.body:
Players need a shirt with sleeves, shorts, socks, suitable shin guards and footwear. Goalkeepers and teams must be distinguishable.

Remove dangerous items, including jewellery. Covering jewellery with tape does not make it acceptable. Check safety again before allowing a corrected player to return.

chapters.title: The referee
chapters.body:
Position yourself to see both the challenge and the surrounding players. Apply advantage only when the offended team can benefit; return to the offence if that benefit does not arise within a few seconds.

Stop for a serious injury. In 2026/27, on-field injury assessment normally means one minute off after the restart, with specified exceptions such as goalkeeper injuries.

chapters.title: Other match officials
chapters.body:
Assistant referees help with boundary decisions, offside and substitutions. Agree on communication and responsibilities before the match.

The referee retains the final decision. Video assistance belongs only to competitions authorised to use it; it is not a feature of every match.

chapters.title: Match duration
chapters.body:
A standard match has two 45-minute halves. Youth and other permitted formats may differ under competition rules.

Add time for substitutions, injuries, disciplinary action, celebrations and other delays. The displayed additional time is a minimum, not a promise to stop at that exact second.

chapters.title: Starting & restarting
chapters.body:
For kick-off, the ball is stationary at the centre mark and enters play when kicked and clearly moving. Opponents remain at least 9.15 m away.

A dropped ball enters play when it touches the ground. Players other than the recipient stay at least 4 m away until then. The recipient depends on the location and possession at the stoppage.

chapters.title: Ball in & out
chapters.body:
The entire ball must cross the boundary, in the air or on the ground, to leave the field. A rebound from a post or flag normally stays in play.

If the ball touches a match official and that touch starts a promising attack, changes possession or sends it directly into goal, stop and restart with a dropped ball.

chapters.title: The match outcome
chapters.body:
A goal requires the whole ball to cross the goal line between the posts and under the bar, without a scoring-team offence.

Competition rules determine how a drawn match is resolved. Penalty shoot-outs are a separate procedure after the match; do not add their kicks to the match score.

chapters.title: Offside
chapters.body:
Position alone is not an offence. At a teammate’s relevant touch, compare the attacker with both the ball and the second-last opponent in the opponents’ half. Arms do not count.

Penalise active involvement: playing the ball, interfering with an opponent or gaining an advantage from a rebound or save. There is no direct offside offence from a throw-in, goal kick or corner.

chapters.title: Fouls & misconduct
chapters.body:
For physical challenges, separate carelessness, recklessness and excessive force. The restart and the disciplinary action answer different questions. Not every ball-to-hand contact is an offence.

A goalkeeper controlling the ball with hands or arms for more than eight seconds concedes a corner. The referee visually counts the final five seconds; bouncing the ball does not reset the count.

chapters.title: Free kicks
chapters.body:
A direct free kick can score against the opponents without another touch; an indirect kick needs another player’s touch. The raised arm signals an indirect kick.

Opponents normally stay 9.15 m away. If a defensive wall has three or more players, attackers stay at least 1 m from it until the ball is in play.

chapters.title: The penalty kick
chapters.body:
Identify the kicker, place the ball on the mark and wait until everyone is correctly positioned. The goalkeeper needs at least part of one foot touching, in line with or behind the goal line at the kick.

The ball must be kicked forward. For an immediate accidental double touch, a scored kick is retaken; a missed kick normally gives an indirect free kick, unless advantage applies.

chapters.title: The throw-in
chapters.body:
Throw with both hands from behind and over the head, facing the field. Part of each foot touches the touchline or ground outside it. Opponents stay at least 2 m from the restart point.

A goal cannot be scored directly. In 2026/27, delaying a throw-in can trigger a five-second visual countdown; exceeding it transfers the throw to the opponents.

chapters.title: The goal kick
chapters.body:
A goal kick usually follows a ball last touched by an attacker going fully over the goal line without a goal. Kick the stationary ball from anywhere in the goal area. It is in play once kicked and clearly moving.

Opponents normally remain outside the penalty area. In 2026/27, exceeding a referee’s five-second delay countdown concedes a corner.

chapters.title: The corner kick
chapters.body:
A corner normally follows the ball leaving over the goal line after a defender’s last touch, without a goal. Other Laws can also award a corner, including goalkeeper time control.

Place the stationary ball in the appropriate corner area; do not move the flag. Opponents stay 9.15 m from the corner arc. A direct goal against the opponents can count.

questions.prompt: The ball still overlaps the touchline. Is it out?
questions.reason: The whole ball must cross the boundary. The line is part of the field.

questions.prompt: The ball bursts during a pass in ordinary play. What now?
questions.reason: A defective ball is replaced. Ordinary play resumes with a dropped ball under the applicable procedure.

questions.prompt: A player deliberately takes 18 seconds to leave for a substitution, with no safety or injury issue. When can the substitute enter?
options: First stoppage after one minute of resumed play
questions.reason: In 2026/27, an unjustified breach of the ten-second exit limit delays the substitute’s entry.

questions.prompt: A player tapes over a necklace. May they wear it?
questions.reason: Jewellery must be removed. Tape does not eliminate the requirement.

questions.prompt: You allow advantage after a foul, but the benefit fails within two seconds. What can you do?
questions.reason: Advantage may be recalled if the expected benefit does not develop within a few seconds.

questions.prompt: An assistant signals offside. Who has the final decision?
questions.reason: Assistants provide information; the referee makes the final decision.

questions.prompt: Three added minutes are shown, then an injury delays play for another minute. Must you stop at 93:00?
options: No, account for the further delay
questions.reason: The displayed added time is a minimum. Further lost time can increase it.

questions.prompt: At a dropped ball, a player kicks it before it touches the ground. What now?
questions.reason: A dropped ball is not in play until it touches the ground.

questions.prompt: The ball hits the referee and possession changes to the other team. What is the restart?
questions.reason: A touch on an official that changes team possession requires a dropped ball.

questions.prompt: A shot is mostly over the goal line but a small part is still above it. Goal?
questions.reason: Every part of the ball must cross the goal line for a goal.

questions.prompt: An attacker receives the ball directly from a teammate’s throw-in beyond the second-last opponent. Offside?
questions.reason: There is no offside offence when receiving directly from a throw-in.

questions.prompt: After the referee’s visible countdown, a goalkeeper still controls the ball with the hands beyond eight seconds. Decision?
questions.reason: Exceeding the eight-second goalkeeper control limit is punished with a corner, not an indirect kick.

questions.prompt: An indirect free kick goes untouched into the opponents’ goal. Decision?
questions.reason: An indirect free kick needs another player’s touch before a goal can count.

questions.prompt: The penalty taker slips, immediately touches the ball accidentally with both feet, and scores. In 2026/27?
questions.reason: An immediate accidental double touch followed by a goal means a retake. Deliberate second touches are different.

questions.prompt: A legal throw-in goes directly into the opponents’ goal without another touch. Decision?
questions.reason: A goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in. Into the opponents’ goal means a goal kick.

questions.prompt: A correctly taken goal kick moves clearly but stays inside the penalty area. Is it in play?
questions.reason: The ball enters play when kicked and clearly moving; it does not have to leave the penalty area.

questions.prompt: A legal corner curls directly into the opponents’ goal. Decision?
questions.reason: A corner may score directly against the opponents if no other offence occurs.
